Resolve affected dependency closures, delegate missing pricing to the downloader outside pricing locks, and publish recoverably before acknowledging locked update notices.

Trust published inputs without re-auditing them; reuse approved closed single-identity assignments on safe monthly continuations, and keep dependency lookup in one incrementally updated index instead of rewriting a universe-sized JSON file.

Delegate missing initial-ticker pricing through the same unlocked downloader handoff as related tickers; when no published range exists, use downloader defaults and resume from its published receipt and notice.

Keep no-download waiting, bounded acquisition, per-ticker failure isolation and publish-before-acknowledge behavior; retain compatible v1 receipt, index and recovery reads without new storage or auditing.
Separate the single-worker guard from brief receipt/index publication locking, allowing completed groups to remain readable during unrelated lineage work.
Use selection, sorted shared pricing locks, and bounded re-selection for all standalone readers; preserve publication recovery and publish-before-acknowledge ordering.

Upgrade only the SQLite protocol header to exclude old lock ordering; reuse v2 publications when all pricing, identity, correlation, report and calendar versions still match, without rewriting their receipts or prices.

Distinguish a missing auxiliary label explicitly rejected by the bars endpoint from failed or incomplete acquisition; continue the normal identity cascade for available inputs without manufacturing empty prices or suppressing candidate identities.

Retain the rejected request and separately acquired metadata in the existing group receipt, discover its downstream dependencies, and include these absent inputs in reverse dependency closure, reader locks and recovery. Later pricing arrival invalidates the publication.

Trust unchanged group generations and identical recorded absence outcomes until pricing changes or explicit metadata refresh; recheck acquisition after range expansion. Preserve existing completed v2/v3 assignments and their pricing boundaries.
